sections.geometry:
Maintain:
- building massing and proportions
- number of floors
- roof geometry
- wall positions
- window and door positions and dimensions
- columns and structural elements
- balconies and terraces
- openings
- stairs
- major architectural features
sections.camera: Preserve the exact camera position, viewing direction, perspective, framing and composition of the reference. Two-point perspective: keep all vertical lines of the building perfectly vertical and parallel in the image; do not tilt or converge them upward.
sections.materials_base: Replace the simple/default model materials with physically realistic materials appropriate to the existing surfaces.

materials_presets.concrete: Prefer architectural concrete: smooth board-formed surfaces, subtle formwork texture, realistic weathering and stains.
materials_presets.wood: Use warm natural wood: visible grain, realistic finish, timber cladding or frames where the design suggests them.
materials_presets.stone: Use natural stone: realistic masonry, joints, texture and color variation.

sections.lighting_base: Create physically plausible natural lighting, realistic indirect illumination, contact shadows, reflections and ambient occlusion. If the sun, sky, or horizon is blocked by the building from this perspective, it must remain occluded behind the architecture — do not remove roofs or walls to show the light source.

lighting_presets.daylight: Clear late-morning daylight: bright natural sun roughly 45–60° above the horizon, crisp short shadows, blue sky with light clouds.
lighting_presets.overcast: Overcast sky: soft diffused daylight, gentle even shadows, muted neutral atmosphere.
lighting_presets.golden_hour: Golden hour: warm low-angle sunlight with the sun roughly 6–10° above the horizon, long soft shadows, warm amber highlights and haze.
lighting_presets.sunset: Sunset: dramatic warm twilight with the sun barely above the horizon (roughly 0–5°), deep orange to pink sky, long shadows falling into dusk.
lighting_presets.night: Night scene: deep blue twilight, moonlight, warm interior light spilling from the windows.

sections.environment_base: Add realistic landscaping, vegetation, sky and environmental details strictly outside the building footprint and only where they do not obscure or modify the building geometry. Never remove or alter walls, roofs, or structural elements to reveal the environment.

environment_presets.none: Keep the surroundings minimal and neutral; do not add vegetation or scenery.
environment_presets.tropical: Tropical setting: dense palm and broadleaf planting, pools, warm humid atmosphere.
environment_presets.urban: Urban setting: streetscape, pavement, neighboring buildings, urban planting.
environment_presets.forest: Forest setting: surrounding trees and woodland framing the site edges.

sections.photography: Make the result resemble a professional architectural photograph with realistic lens characteristics, exposure, depth, texture and color response.

style_presets.editorial: Editorial treatment: slightly muted color grade, magazine-style composition, restrained detail, quiet sky.
style_presets.minimal: Minimal treatment: sparse scene, near-empty surroundings, soft diffused light, clean restrained palette, nothing decorative competing with the architecture.
style_presets.atmospheric: Atmospheric treatment: moody light, soft haze and depth, dramatic sky, cinematic color grade while the architecture stays clearly legible.

sections.settings_scope:
SETTINGS SCOPE — read carefully:
The finish, season, weather, sky and color settings above describe surface finish, atmosphere, surroundings and color treatment only. They never license changes to the building itself: do not add, remove, move, resize or redesign any architectural element, opening, roof, wall, window, door or structural feature, and do not reinterpret the architecture to match an atmosphere setting. Where any instruction above appears to conflict with the reference model, the reference model wins.

fidelity.strict:
ABSOLUTE RESTRICTION:
Do not redesign the building.
Do not modify its geometry.
Do not change dimensions or proportions.
Do not add or remove architectural elements.
Do not change the number or position of windows, doors, floors, columns, balconies, roofs or openings.
Never produce cutaways, open-air conversions, or transparent walls: all solid roofs and walls must remain 100% solid and opaque.
If the building occludes the sun, sky, or environment from this camera angle, the background must remain hidden behind the architecture — never remove or modify structure to reveal environment or lighting.

The final image should be recognizable as the exact same building shown in the reference, only rendered as if it physically existed and had been professionally photographed.
Geometry fidelity is more important than visual creativity.
fidelity.medium:
RESTRICTION:
Preserve the building core: massing, proportions, floor count, roof geometry and major openings. Surface materials, color, landscaping and atmosphere may be interpreted more freely while the architecture stays recognizable.
fidelity.creative:
GUIDANCE:
Preserve the overall massing and proportions of the reference, but freely reimagine materials, details, environment and atmosphere for an artistic result.
